RAII helper that creates a temporary directory in its constructor and, if autodelete is true, removes it in the destructor. Exposes the created directory path via path(). Exact creation/removal mechanics are defined in the implementation and not visible here.

RAII helper that temporarily switches the process timezone to tz if available; on destruction, restores the previous timezone. available() reports whether the requested timezone could be set. Relies on set_tz and timezone_available (declared elsewhere).

A value-type struct representing an email contact within the Mu namespace. Holds email, optional display name, contact type (header field category), message date, whether personal, occurrence frequency, and timestamp. Provides comparison operators for relevance sorting, validation and display helpers, and mapping to Field::Id. Details about lifetime are standard value semantics; no special destruction requirements.
Strongly-typed scoped enum inside Mu::Contact identifying the contact field category: none/sender/from/reply-to/to/cc/bcc. Underlying type is char with mnemonic letter codes.

Strongly scoped enumeration representing message priority levels within the Mu namespace. Underlying type is char and values map to 'l', 'n', and 'h'. Used with helper functions to convert to/from characters and names.

objects.definition:
enum struct Flags {
	None = 0, /**< No flags */
	/**
	 * next 6 are seen in the file-info part of maildir message file
	 * names, ie., in a name like "1234345346:2,<fileinfo>",
	 * <fileinfo> consists of zero or more of the following
	 * characters (in ascii order)
	 */
	Draft   = 1 << 0, /**< A draft message */
	Flagged = 1 << 1, /**< A flagged message */
	Passed  = 1 << 2, /**< A passed (forwarded) message */
	Replied = 1 << 3, /**< A replied message */
	Seen    = 1 << 4, /**< A seen (read) message */
	Trashed = 1 << 5, /**< A trashed message */

	/**
	 * decides on cur/ or new/ in the maildir
	 */
	New = 1 << 6, /**< A new message */

	/**
	 * content flags -- not visible in the filename, but used for
	 * searching
	 */
	Signed        = 1 << 7, /**< Cryptographically signed */
	Encrypted     = 1 << 8, /**< Encrypted */
	HasAttachment = 1 << 9, /**< Has an attachment */

	Unread = 1 << 10, /**< Unread; pseudo-flag, only for queries, so we can
			   * search for flag:unread, which is equivalent to
			   * 'flag:new OR NOT flag:seen' */
	/**
	 * other content flags
	 */
	MailingList = 1 << 11, /**< A mailing-list message */
	Personal    = 1 << 12, /**< A personal message (i.e., at least one of the
				* contact fields contains a personal address) */
	Calendar    = 1 << 13, /**< A calendar invitation */
	/*
	 * <private>
	 */
	_final_ = 1 << 14
};
MU_ENABLE_BITOPS(Flags);
objects.description: Strongly-typed bitmask enum describing message flags used by Mu. MU_ENABLE_BITOPS(Flags) enables bit operations like |, &, ~, any_of/none_of helpers. Values cover maildir filename flags, content flags, and a pseudo Unread flag; _final_ is a sentinel upper bound.
Categorization enum for Flags, distinguishing file, location, content, or pseudo flags.

Metadata record describing a single message flag: the Flags value, a unique shortcut character, its canonical name, category, and a short description. Provides a constexpr helper to get the lowercase shortcut.

Provides utilities to derive Xapian prefix/term and to query characteristics (searchable, range, value, etc.). Construction is typically via aggregate initialization in the Fields array; destruction is trivial. Details about xapian_term implementation are external to this header.

Mu::Document is a wrapper around Xapian::Document that models an email message record in the Mu database. It provides methods to add/remove fields, contacts, flags, and priority; retrieve values; and access a cached S-expression representation. Lifetime: holds a mutable Xapian::Document by value. Construction: either default with options or from an existing Xapian::Document and options. Destruction triggers xapian_document() to ensure the S-expression side-effect is applied. Unknowns: exact behavior of xapian_document(), Field, Contacts, Priority, Flags, and Sexp are defined elsewhere.
Scoped enum of option flags for Mu::Document behavior. Currently supports None and SupportNgrams for CJK/ngram support. Bit-ops are enabled via MU_ENABLE_BITOPS(Document::Options).

A C++ class representing a MIME message part within namespace Mu. It wraps and manages access to an underlying MimeObject (held via unique_ptr) and provides APIs to query filenames, MIME type, size, disposition, and security properties, as well as to extract decoded content to a string or file. The actual MimeObject definition is not present in this header; users must include mu-mime-object.hh for direct interaction with MimeObject.

Holds split components of a message path: directory (e.g., cur/ or new/ parent), filename, and a boolean indicating whether the message resides in new/ (is_new).

Wrapper for GMimeContentType exposing media/subtype, full mime type, type checks, and parameters.
Wrapper for GMimeStream providing write/reset/flush and factory helpers for memory, filter, or existing streams.
Wrapper for GMimeDataWrapper. Can write its data to a MimeStream.
Wrapper for GMimeCertificate, providing enums for key/digest/trust/validity and accessors for certificate metadata and times.
Wrapper for GMimeSignature with status flags, validity times, and access to the associated certificate.
Wrapper for GMimeDecryptResult. Provides access to recipients, signatures, chosen cipher and MDC digest algo, and an optional session key.
Wrapper for GMimeCryptoContext. Provides constructors for GPG or arbitrary protocol, protocol queries, key import, and a password request callback hook.
Common base wrapper for all GMime object kinds with header access, serialization to stream/string/file, type queries, and a callback type for traversal.
Wrapper for a top-level GMimeMessage with constructors from file/text, access to headers like subject/message-id/date, MIME part, contacts, references, and recursive traversal.
Wrapper for a GMimePart (leaf MIME entity). Provides attachment checks, metadata headers, content access, content size/serialization, and enums for transfer encoding and OpenPGP data type.
Wrapper for a GMimeMessagePart (a message/rfc822 part) with access to the embedded MimeMessage.
Wrapper for application/pkcs7-mime parts with accessor for the S/MIME content subtype.
Wrapper for GMimeMultipart with helpers to access specific signed/encrypted parts and recursive traversal.
Wrapper for GMimeMultipartEncrypted providing decryption with flags and returning the decrypted object plus decrypt result.
Wrapper for GMimeMultipartSigned providing signature verification with optional flags, yielding a list of MimeSignature.

Core email message class in namespace Mu. Wraps metadata and operations around a message stored in a Mu::Document, supports file-backed or text-backed creation, lazy loading of MIME content, labels/tags/flags management, threading info, and provides conversions to S-expression. Uses PIMPL via Message::Private. Construction is via static factory methods returning Result<Message>. Destruction and copy are not defined; move operations are supported. Details of underlying Document, Flags, Priority, Contacts, etc., are external to this header.

Configuration property descriptor used by Mu::Config. Encapsulates metadata about a single property (identifier, type, flags, name, default value, description). Primary store class managing a Xapian-backed message database. Uses PIMPL via nested Private to hide implementation.
Lightweight snapshot of store statistics: total messages, last modification time, and last indexing time. Returned by Store::statistics().

Main class that abstracts the indexing process for a message store. Provides lifecycle (start/stop), status (is_running, progress, completed), and owns a hidden implementation (Pimpl via Private). Constructed with a Store reference. Destruction and ownership of internal resources are managed internally. Details of threading and exact behavior are not defined here.

Configuration struct for Indexer::start controlling what the indexing run should do: scan for new messages, clean removed messages, ignore .noupdate sentinels, and perform lazy checks based on ctime. Default-initialized with scan and cleanup enabled, others disabled.

Thread-safe progress snapshot for the most recent indexing job. Exposes atomic counters for running, checked, updated, and removed items, and a helper reset() to clear state. Returned by Indexer::progress() as a const reference.

Alias for an unordered set of std::string used within the Mu namespace to collect unique string identifiers (e.g., thread or message IDs).

Strongly scoped enumeration for parser feature flags used by Mu's query parsing and Xapian query construction. S-expression node/list type used to represent token streams and parse trees of queries. Exact structure is defined elsewhere (utils/mu-sexp.hh). Used as return type of process_query and parse_query.
Template instantiation representing either a successful Xapian::Query or an error, returned by make_xapian_query. The Result template is defined elsewhere (utils/mu-result.hh).
Message store abstraction providing data required to resolve wildcard/regex queries when building Xapian queries. Defined elsewhere (mu-store.hh). Appears here as a referenced parameter type only.

Per-document aggregate used for sorting and threading metadata of a search result. Contains flags, date/subject keys, thread topology, and helpers. Includes a nested Flags enum with bit-ops enabled.

Mu::Server implements the mu server used by mu4e. It accepts s-expression commands via invoke and writes responses through a user-supplied Output callback. Internally uses a PIMPL Private managed by unique_ptr. Construction requires a Store reference, Options, and an Output. Destruction releases internal resources. Details of behavior beyond this interface are not exposed here.

Abstract interface for key/value metadata backends. Provides get/set, read-only query, iteration via a callback, and two well-known key names. Implemented by MemDb and XapianDb.

In-memory implementation of MetadataIface backed by an unordered_map. Useful for tests or ephemeral storage; supports optional read-only mode flag but does not enforce it internally beyond reporting via read_only().

functions.description: Applies a sequence of label deltas to an existing set of labels and returns a pair: the updated unique label set and the effective changes (a filtered DeltaLabelVec). Deltas are applied in order with "last one wins" semantics. The resulting labels contain no duplicates and order is not guaranteed to be preserved. The effective changes exclude redundant additions (adding a label already present) and removals (removing a label not present).

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: plain text string
# Goal: generate interesting, valid UTF-8/byte strings that exercise
# - fmt-friendly payloads
# - small/medium sizes
# - visible ASCII, punctuation, whitespace, unicode, control removal cases, etc.
# Constraints: <= 4096 bytes

VISIBLE_ASCII = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x20, 0x7f))
WHITESPACE = '\t\n\r \f\v'
PUNCT = string.punctuation

# Some useful Unicode blocks/samples to exercise UTF-8 handling
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    # Latin with diacritics
    "Café naïve façade coöperate résumé jalapeño piñata",
    # Greek
    " Ελληνικά: αβγδεζηθικλμνξοπρστυφχψω ",
    # Cyrillic
    " Кириллица: Привет мир ",
    # Arabic (RTL)
    " العربية: مرحبا بالعالم ",
    # Hebrew (RTL)
    " עברית: שלום עולם ",
    # Devanagari (Hindi)
    " देवनागरी: नमस्ते दुनिया ",
    # Thai (unbroken script)
    " ไทย: สวัสดีชาวโลก ",
    # CJK (Chinese, Japanese, Korean)
    " 中文：你好，世界  日本語：こんにちは世界  한국어: 안녕하세요 세계 ",
    # Emojis
    " Emojis: 😀😂👍🔥✨🚀❤️🍕🐍🎉 ",
]

FORMAT_TEMPLATES = [
    "int:{}",
    "str:{}",
    "mix:{} {}",
    "float:{:.3f}",
    "payload:{}",
    "noop:{}",
    "dbg n:{}",
    "dbg s:{}",
    "info n:{}",
    "info s:{}",
    "msg n:{}",
    "msg s:{}",
    "warn n:{}",
    "warn s:{}",
    "crit n:{}",
    "crit s:{}",
    "err n:{}",
    "err s:{}",
    "print n:{}",
    "print s:{}",
    "println n:{}",
    "println s:{}",
    "stderr n:{}",
    "stderr s:{}",
    "stderrln n:{}",
    "stderrln s:{}",
]

MAILDIR_FLAG_SHORTCUTS = "DFPRS TNEWSEHAUMLPC".lower().replace(' ', '')
# Above is a superset; actual set will be filtered by the target, but
# composing from valid-looking letters helps build absolute/delta exprs.


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    pool = VISIBLE_ASCII + WHITESPACE
    return ''.join(r.choice(pool) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_unicode(r: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    base = r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    # Mix base with some ascii/punct
    tail = _rand_ascii(r, max(0, n - len(base)))
    return (base + tail)[:n]


def _make_regex_pattern(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Safe, PCRE-ish patterns
    parts = [
        r"^.*$",
        r"\b[a-zA-Z]+\b",
        r"[0-9]{1,3}",
        r"foo|bar|baz",
        r"(hello).*?(world)",
        r"\w+@\w+\.[a-z]{2,4}",
    ]
    return r.choice(parts)


def _make_flag_absolute(r: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(r.choice(MAILDIR_FLAG_SHORTCUTS) for _ in range(max(1, length)))


def _make_flag_delta(r: random.Random, pairs: int) -> str:
    expr = []
    for _ in range(max(1, pairs)):
        op = r.choice(['+', '-'])
        sc = r.choice(MAILDIR_FLAG_SHORTCUTS)
        expr.append(op + sc)
    return ''.join(expr)


def _make_join_payload(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build comma-separated small tokens to exercise join
    n_parts = r.randint(1, 8)
    parts: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n_parts):
        slen = r.randint(0, 12)
        parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, slen))
    sepa = r.choice([",", "|", "/", "::", " · "])
    return sepa.join(parts)


def _make_priority_token(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # valid tokens or invalid for negative path
    choices = ["low", "normal", "high", "l", "n", "h"]
    if r.random() < 0.75:
        return r.choice(choices)
    else:
        return r.choice(choices) + "_"  # invalid


def _make_contact_email(r: random.Random) -> str:
    user = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 10)))
    dom = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)))
    tld = r.choice(["com", "net", "org", "io", "dev"])
    return f"{user}@{dom}.{tld}"


def _make_format_instance(r: random.Random) -> str:
    tpl = r.choice(FORMAT_TEMPLATES)
    # we just emit the template text itself for logging; fuzzer supplies args separately
    return tpl


def _mix_sections(sections: List[str], r: random.Random, target_max: int) -> str:
    r.shuffle(sections)
    out = "\n".join(sections)
    if len(out) > target_max:
        out = out[:target_max]
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    max_total = 4096

    # Build multiple themed sections separated by newlines to serve many stubs:
    sections: List[str] = []

    # 1) Generic UTF-8 payloads
    sections.append(_rand_ascii(r, r.randint(0, 64)))
    sections.append(_rand_unicode(r, r.randint(32, 256)))

    # 2) Regex pattern for Mu::Regex::make
    sections.append("/re/ " + _make_regex_pattern(r))

    # 3) fmt format templates used by mu_format/mu_* logging wrappers
    fmt_bundle = [ _make_format_instance(r) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)) ]
    sections.append("\n".join(fmt_bundle))

    # 4) Join payload
    sections.append(_make_join_payload(r))

    # 5) Maildir flags absolute and delta expressions
    sections.append("flags_abs:" + _make_flag_absolute(r, r.randint(1, 10)))
    sections.append("flags_delta:" + _make_flag_delta(r, r.randint(1, 6)))

    # 6) Priority tokens
    pr_tokens = [ _make_priority_token(r) for _ in range(3) ]
    sections.append("prio:" + ",".join(pr_tokens))

    # 7) Contacts-like lines (name, email)
    contact_lines = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)):
        name = _rand_unicode(r, r.randint(0, 24)).strip()
        email = _make_contact_email(r)
        contact_lines.append(f"{name} <{email}>")
    sections.append("\n".join(contact_lines))

    # 8) Sexp-like tokens for Sexp parse-related paths (not strict, but useful strings)
    sexp_snippets = [
        "(test :arg \"value\" :n 42)",
        "(:flag t)",
        "(cmd :vec (\"a\" \"b\" \"c\"))",
        "(nil)",
    ]
    sections.append("\n".join(sexp_snippets))

    # 9) Random long unicode paragraph to stress utf8_clean/flatten
    sections.append(_rand_unicode(r, r.randint(128, 512)))

    # 10) Some edge whitespace/control presence
    ctrl = "\x00\x01\x02" + "\n\r\t" + "  "
    sections.append(ctrl + _rand_ascii(r, r.randint(8, 32)) + ctrl)

    data = _mix_sections(sections, r, max_total)
    return data.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
